h1: Banpu Koh Chang Resort — Wooden Beachfront Bungalows, Adults Only, with the Sand Right Outside Your Door
intro: On White Sand Beach (Haad Sai Khao), the liveliest beach on Koh Chang, Banpu Koh Chang Resort is a long-standing wooden bungalow resort that claimed its spot right on the sand back before this beach filled up with places to stay · Two things to know before you book: one — these days it is adults only, so families with young kids can't book here · two — the appeal here is the beachfront location and the bungalow-in-a-green-garden feel, not luxury. Rooms range from traditional wooden bungalows (some old and dark) to brighter rooms in a newer building · The strong points are stepping straight from your room onto the sand and being a few minutes' walk from restaurants, a convenience store and the bar strip · Rooms start at around THB 2,800/night in normal season · Overall score about 8.2 from real guest reviews.

body.html: The first thing worth making clear up front, because it directly affects your decision: these days Banpu Koh Chang Resort is adults only · If you're planning a Koh Chang trip as a family with young kids, this place won't take your booking, and you'll need to look at another resort on White Sand Beach instead · But if you're a couple, a group of friends, or travelling solo and you want a quiet beachfront vibe with no kids running around, this is exactly why many people pick it over the big family resorts · Being adults only means the overall mood is more relaxed and private than you'd usually get at this price · Before you book, it's worth checking the minimum-age policy with the resort again, since rules like this vary from place to place — and if you're coming as a group with both adults and teens, you'll want to avoid a surprise at check-in.

To give you the big picture before the details — Banpu is a small-to-mid-size resort, with bungalows and rooms spread through a mature garden where the trees have grown in enough to shade most of the grounds. It's not a high-rise or a sprawling complex · The character here is an old-school beachfront resort that's about location and atmosphere more than luxury — the kind that European visitors who come back to Koh Chang year after year know well and like · The people who'll be happy here are the ones who understand from the start that they're coming to sleep right by the beach, get around the White Sand Beach area easily on foot, and live simply by the sea — not for fancy facilities or modern-design rooms. Set your expectations right from the start and the odds of leaving happy are high.

What's kept Banpu on White Sand Beach all these years is its genuinely beachfront location · The resort sits toward the middle-to-southern end of White Sand Beach, and it's just a few steps through the garden from your bungalow to the beach chairs and the sand · White Sand Beach is the longest beach on the island and the most fully serviced, so having a place right on the sand here is worth a lot — wake up and you can walk straight in for a swim, and in the evening you can watch the sun set into the sea to the west from right in front of the resort · The honest catch is that the beach in front of the resort is narrow and has more underwater rocks than the northern stretch of White Sand Beach, especially at high tide. Plenty of real reviews say the same thing — if you want a wide stretch of sand you can wade into comfortably, walk a bit further up the beach to the north, or wear water shoes to protect your feet from the rocks · The upside of being on this stretch is that you're close to the restaurants, the convenience store and the bar strip in the middle of the beach, all an easy walk away — no need to rely on a car or rent a motorbike the way you would staying on a beach further out. For people who don't drive on the island, this convenience matters more than you'd think.

The rooms here fall into two clearly different characters, and this is the thing most worth understanding before you book · The first group is the traditional wooden bungalows that carry the feel of old-Koh-Chang resorts — dark wood, tucked into a shady garden. The charm is in the atmosphere, but real reviews agree that some of them are old, dark and dated, with bathrooms and furniture that have seen a lot of use · The second group is the rooms in the renovated building, which are far brighter, airier and more modern; people who land in this group tend to review in a positive tone · The honest advice is that if room freshness matters to you, ask specifically for a newer-building or renovated room when you book — don't leave it to chance, because the gap between the two groups is big enough to shape how the whole trip feels.

"The location really is the star — you walk from your room straight onto the beach, have your morning coffee by the sea, and at night the restaurants and the 7-Eleven are right there. Just make sure you get a newer-building room. The old wooden bungalow my friend stayed in looked a lot more worn out."

Every room has the basics covered for a beachfront place at this level — air conditioning, a fridge, a TV, a safe, and a balcony or porch to sit out on; some rooms have tea- and coffee-making gear and wooden floors that give a warm feel · The rooms aren't huge, in keeping with the beachfront-bungalow style, but they're enough for a couple or a traveller who's out and about most of the day · The shared area has a small outdoor pool with a sea view and a poolside bar, and here it has to be said straight that the pool is fairly small for the size of the resort — better for cooling off than for serious swimming, and it can feel crowded when it's full; with the beach right there, plenty of people choose the sea over the pool anyway · So the appeal of the shared area isn't the pool but sitting with a drink looking out at the sea in a mature, leafy garden that feels natural and shaded · The poolside bar and the lounging spots by the beach are the corners many couples say they like best, especially in the evening when the light softens and the sea breeze comes in.

Food is where the resort earns more praise than you'd expect at this price · The beachfront restaurant serves Thai food, Western dishes and fresh seafood, with seafood BBQ by the sea on some nights · What real reviews mention most is the buffet breakfast — plenty of choice and tastier than you'd expect for the price, especially the Thai dishes, which many people say are done better than at comparable hotels · Sitting down to breakfast looking out at the sea in the morning is something many reviews call a highlight · For lunch and dinner, if you want a change of scene you can walk out to the middle of White Sand Beach, where there are plenty of seafood spots, local eateries and international restaurants to choose from, all within walking distance.

On service, most of the feedback leans positive · The staff are friendly, warm and helpful, and many reviews praise the attentiveness and the easygoing, informal care that fits the relaxed character of the place · There's a tour desk to help arrange snorkelling trips, transfers and other activities on the island · The desk is open 24 hours, with a safe, a currency-exchange service and an easy check-out · The thing to keep in mind is that this is a small resort, so big-resort facilities — a full gym, a full-service spa, a kids' club — aren't here. But that lines up with the adults-only stance and its focus on keeping things simple by the beach.

The things worth saying straight so you can decide with the full picture · One — some of the old wooden bungalows are worn and dark; if you land in this group without asking ahead, you may be disappointed · Two — the pool is small for the size of the resort and can get crowded in high season · Three — the beach in front of the resort on this stretch is narrow and has underwater rocks, not ideal if you want a long wade into the water · Four — it's in a lively area, and some nights you may hear noise from nearby restaurants and bars; anyone who needs total quiet should pick a room set further back or consider a resort on another beach · Five — some reviews feel the high-season price is on the high side given the state of the old bungalows, so value depends on which room you get and what rate you book it at.

The location is on White Sand Beach on the northwestern side of Koh Chang, the first beach you reach after the ferry and the one with the most shops and services on the island · From the ferry pier (Ao Sapparot / Centre Point) it's about a 10–15 min drive · It's a few minutes' walk to the convenience store, restaurants and the bar strip in the middle of the beach · Klong Prao Beach is about 15 min away and Klong Plu Waterfall about 20 min · Getting to Koh Chang means taking a road trip to Laem Ngop pier in Trat, then a ferry across that takes about 30–45 min, then a songthaew or taxi on the island to White Sand Beach, which is the closest beach to the pier · Scores across platforms span a wide range: Trip.com gives it around 9.1 from a small number of reviews, while Booking.com is around 8.1 and the Koh Chang specialist site iamkohchang gives it around 7.7 · Averaging all the voices lands at about 8.2, a number that matches the character of this place: strong on location, breakfast and service, but dragged down by the state of the old bungalows and the small pool · A spread this wide is a sign that experiences differ a lot depending on the room you get — which underlines, again, choosing your room carefully when you book.

To weigh up the value properly, you have to compare it with its neighbours on White Sand Beach · In a similar price range, a resort like KC Grande Resort & Spa offers newer rooms, several pools including a rooftop one, and full-service resort facilities — but it's a big resort with more people and it isn't adults only · Where Banpu still has the edge is the private, quieter bungalow-in-a-garden feel and a location you can walk everywhere from · So value here comes down to two things mainly: the rate you book and the room you get — if you land a newer-building room at a normal-season rate of around THB 2,800–3,500, it's good value for the beachfront location, but if you end up paying a high-season rate for an old wooden bungalow, the sense of value drops straight away. Some of the lower-scoring reviews tend to come from that second case.

The straight summary: Banpu Koh Chang Resort suits couples, groups of friends or adult travellers who value a beachfront location and the convenience of walking everywhere over luxurious rooms · If you can land a newer-building room at a normal-season rate, it's good value for sleeping right on White Sand Beach in the middle of everything · But if you expect every room to be modern and beautiful, a big pool you can actually swim laps in, or you're travelling as a family with young kids (which this place doesn't take), a White Sand Beach resort like KC Grande or a Klong Prao Beach resort will fit what you're after more closely.

honestSummary: Banpu Koh Chang Resort stands out for its beachfront location on White Sand Beach — sand at your door and everything within walking distance — plus a breakfast and service that earn praise, all in an adults-only bungalow-in-a-garden setting · But understand that the rooms split between old wooden bungalows that are dark and dated and newer-building rooms that are far brighter, the pool is small, and the beach in front of the resort is narrow with rocks — so ask for a renovated room when you book.
honestChecks: If you're travelling as a family with young kids — this place is adults only and won't take your booking → choose a family resort on White Sand Beach like KC Grande or a Klong Prao Beach resort instead.

If room freshness matters to you — some of the old wooden bungalows are dark and dated, very different from the newer-building rooms → ask specifically for a renovated or newer-building room when you book, don't leave it to chance.

If you want a big pool or a wide sandy beach to wade into comfortably — the pool here is small, and the beach in front on this stretch is narrow with underwater rocks → factor this in, or walk a bit up the beach to the north for a wider stretch of sand.

tips.body: The breakfast buffet earns praise for its Thai food, and eating it while looking out at the sea in the morning is a highlight many reviews call out. Try coming early before it gets busy.

tips.title: Walk up the beach north for wider sand
tips.body: The beach in front of the resort on this stretch is narrow and rocky. Walk up the beach toward the northern end of White Sand Beach and you'll find a wider stretch of sand that's easier to wade into.

tips.body: It's in a lively area, and some nights you'll hear noise from the restaurants and bars. If noise makes it hard for you to sleep, ask for a room set further back from the road.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Banpu Koh Chang Resort, Koh Chang

faq.q: Does Banpu Koh Chang Resort take children · is it really adults only?
faq.a: These days it's adults only · Families with young kids can't book here · This stance keeps the resort calm and private, well suited to couples, groups of friends and adult travellers · If you're coming as a family, choose a White Sand Beach resort that takes children instead, such as KC Grande Resort & Spa.

faq.q: Is Banpu Koh Chang Resort on the beach · what's the beach like?
faq.a: It's genuinely beachfront, sitting toward the middle-to-southern end of White Sand Beach — walk from your room through the garden straight onto the sand · But the beach in front of the resort is fairly narrow and has more underwater rocks than the northern stretch of White Sand Beach, especially at high tide · If you want a wide stretch of sand to wade into comfortably, walk a bit up the beach to the north.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Banpu Koh Chang Resort · which should I choose?
faq.a: The rooms split into two very different groups · Traditional wooden bungalows that have atmosphere but where some are old and dark, and rooms in the renovated building that are brighter and more modern · It's best to ask specifically for a newer-building or renovated room when you book so you don't end up in an old bungalow by accident.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Banpu Koh Chang Resort?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 2,800/night for a Superior room in normal season · In high season, family/suite rooms can rise to around THB 5,500, while low season has noticeably cheaper deals · Prices swing quite a bit by season, so it's worth comparing several platforms before you book.

faq.q: Is Banpu Koh Chang Resort easy to get to · where is it on Koh Chang?
faq.a: It's on White Sand Beach (Haad Sai Khao), the first and liveliest beach on Koh Chang · From the ferry pier it's about a 10–15 min drive · It's a few minutes' walk to the restaurants, the convenience store and the bar strip in the middle of the beach. Klong Prao Beach is about 15 min away and Klong Plu Waterfall about 20 min.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Banpu Koh Chang Resort?
faq.a: The things to factor in are that the pool is too small for the size of the resort, some of the old wooden bungalows look dated, and it's in a lively area where some nights you'll hear noise from the restaurants and bars · The points that earn consistent praise are the location, the breakfast buffet and the friendly staff · It suits people who value a beachfront location and convenience over luxurious rooms.
